messages:
Jordan: Hey team — Acme (prospect) just asked for a 12-month export of our audit logs for an upcoming review. They want PII redacted, evidence of KMS usage (key ID + envelope wrap), and per-request RBAC context (route, token id). Can we confirm what we can deliver and any gaps?
Sasha: We can generate an export from the audit-service S3 bucket. It contains event json with route and subject. PII redaction is supported at ingest, but it depends on the redact rules. Do we have their mask list? :thinking_face: 
Jordan: They're asked us to redact email, phone, and full prompt text. They also want a separate manifest showing which KMS key encrypted the archive.
Kevin: For KMS we can sign an export manifest that includes the CMK id used to wrap the archive. We currently use a tenant-wrapped envelope per-customer for Private, hosted uses our service key. If Acme requires their BYOK CMK, that's only supported for Private right now.
Irene: Two practical items: 1) route-level RBAC context — we log route names but not always the token id in plaintext. We store token fingerprint for privacy. 2) Redaction: we have a pipeline job that can apply deterministic redaction based on regex rules; it runs during export.
Marta: Sales asked for a timeline to tell Acme. They need the export and evidence by EOW next week if possible. What is ETA?
Sasha: ETA depends on 1) whether they accept token fingerprint vs token id, and 2) BYOK requirement. If they accept fingerprint and our signed manifest, we can do a scoped export in ~3 business days. If they require their CMK to wrap, we need Private deployment or engage infra for a one-off key-wrapping run — estimate 10-14 days.
Jordan: Okay. Two clarifications: can the audit export contain a verifiable chain-of-custody (hashes, signatures)? And can we include a human-readable redaction summary?
Kevin: Yes — we can produce: (a) gzipped export files, (b) a manifest.json with sha256 for each file, signed by our infra key, and (c) a redaction-log.csv with counts of redacted fields per file. Example manifest: ```{\n  "files": [{ "path": "audit-2025-10-01.gz", "sha256": "..." }],\n  "signed_by": "infra-export-v1",\n  "kms_wrap": "arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd-1234"\n}```
Irene: Note: the redaction-log.csv will include only metrics (counts) not the redacted values. If Acme wants the actual original prompts for their review, we need an E3-approved data access request and retention justification.
Jordan: Good call. Also security question: if we include token fingerprints only, can they map them back to their internal user ids? They will want correlation for audit purposes.
Sasha: They can, if we provide a lookup table mapping fingerprint -> customer-visible user id. That table is PII-bearing and requires a JIT (just-in-time) access flow. We should gate with a signed NDA or an auditor access agreement.
Marta: Acme's compliance lead said auditor will be internal, not a third-party. They asked for direct mapping. We should confirm legal.
Kevin: From infra side: generating the export and signing manifest is straightforward. Steps: spin export job for date-range, run redact pipeline with their regex, run sha256+sign, upload to their S3 (if cross-account) with envelope encryption. For cross-account S3 upload with customer's KMS, we need their AWS account id and a grant for our service principal.
Jordan: Can someone list the exact artifacts we'll produce (names + brief formats) so I can tell Acme?
Irene: Artifact list: 1) export-YYYYMMDD-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz (gzipped newline-delimited JSON events), 2) manifest-YYYYMMDD.json (sha256 checksums + signatures), 3) redaction-summary-YYYYMMDD.csv (counts by event type/field), 4) access-instructions.txt (S3 bucket + path + expiry), 5) optionally lookup-table.csv (fingerprint -> customer_user_id) — requires formal approval.
SecBot: Reminder: any transfer of PII in exports must be recorded in the data-transfer register and trigger a KMS key-rotation check per policy SEC-ROT-3.
Jordan: Thanks. Action items: Sasha to confirm whether fingerprint mapping is acceptable; Kevin to validate cross-account KMS wrap flow and estimate time; Irene to draft export artifact template; Marta to confirm legal/auditor agreement with Acme. ETA: Sasha/Kevin/Irene to update by EOD tomorrow. Marta to loop in legal.
Sasha: Ack. I'll ping Acme for the exact mask list and whether fingerprint mapping is okay.
Kevin: I'll run a dry-run export on a small date range tomorrow to validate pipeline and produce a sample manifest.
Irene: I'll author the artifact templates and redact rules doc.
Marta: I'll confirm auditor type and push for the NDA.
Jordan: Awesome. If anyone hits a blocker (BYOK or retention policy conflict), flag here and we'll escalate to infra + legal. :thumbsup:
